reference: Intel Core i7-12700K, single-thread rates measured on Linux. 100 points = reference single-thread rate.

overall.normNotes: Normalizers are the reference CPU's expected quad- and multi-core scores. multi=1000 is modeled from measured per-kernel scaling of a Ryzen 9 9950X3D (8 P-cores with SMT + 4 E-cores) and cross-checked against public all-core ratios (~980-985); provisional until a full-thread i7-12700K result is measured.

gpu.status: provisional: reference projected from RTX 4060 specifications at the efficiency measured on a real RTX 5090 (~69% of rated FP32 and bandwidth); will be replaced by measured RTX 4060 results
gpu.reference: NVIDIA GeForce RTX 4060 (projected). 100 points = reference GPU.

disk.status: provisional: projected for a mainstream PCIe 4.0 NVMe SSD (Samsung 980 PRO class) under this benchmark's settings; will be recalibrated from real results
disk.reference: Mainstream PCIe 4.0 NVMe SSD. 100 points = reference drive.

profiles.note: Profiles reweight the same measured sub-scores; they never change measurements. 'everyday' equals each component's headline score.

gaming.label: Gaming
gaming.rationale: Most games are limited by a few fast threads, but current engines use 6-8 cores, so all-core throughput still counts.

everyday.label: Everyday
everyday.rationale: Browsing, office work and light content creation: responsiveness plus occasional all-core work.

workstation.label: Workstation
workstation.rationale: Rendering, compiling, encoding and simulation scale across every core.

gaming.label: Gaming
gaming.rationale: Load times are dominated by reads: large assets sequentially, many small files randomly.

everyday.label: Everyday
everyday.rationale: Booting, launching apps and general use: low-queue random reads matter most.

workstation.label: Workstation
workstation.rationale: Large files and parallel I/O: video editing, datasets, VMs and build caches.

calibration.note: Reference hardware for each provisional value. Once enough accepted results exist, medians from these components replace the provisional numbers (reviewed, committed change; stored results are rescored).

builds.note: A build's score for a profile is a weighted geometric mean of its parts' scores for that profile (CPU and storage use their profile scores, the GPU its single score). Missing parts are left out and the remaining weights rescaled. When a build has several drives, the first (system) drive counts.
